svg.title: The difference quotient as a sequence of algebra jobs
svg.desc: Every first-principles derivative follows the same pipeline: shift the input, subtract the complete outputs, factor the input change, cancel only after factoring, and then take the limit. Treat the quotient as a workflow, not as one giant line of algebra. The factor h appears because f(a+h)-f(a) measures a change caused by an input change of h . It is legal to cancel that factor while h 0 ; the limit is then taken afterward. The order matters. Every first-principles derivative follows the same pipeline: shift the input, subtract the complete outputs, factor the input change, cancel only after factoring, and then take the limit. Treat the quotient as a workflow, not as one giant line of algebra. The factor h appears because f(a+h)-f(a) measures a change caused by an input change of h . It is legal to cancel that factor while h 0 ; the limit is then taken afterward. The order matters. The visual uses labeled positions, solid and dashed line styles, and written descriptions so the difference quotient as a sequence of algebra jobs does not depend on color. Caption: Every first-principles derivative follows the same pipeline: shift the input, subtract the complete outputs, factor the input change, cancel only after factoring, and then take the limit. Reading order: shift-box: Labeled box: 1. Shift input: f(a + h).; subtract-box: Labeled box: 2. Subtract complete outputs.; quotient-box: Labeled box: 3. Divide by input change h.; factor-box: Labeled box: 4. Factor the numerator.; cancel-box: Labeled box: 5. Cancel only while h is not 0.; limit-box: Labeled box: 6. Then take the limit h to 0.; a1-arrow: Arrow preserves the instructional reading order.; a2-arrow: Arrow preserves the instructional reading order.; a3-arrow: Arrow preserves the instructional reading order.; a4-arrow: Arrow preserves the instructional reading order.; a5-arrow: Arrow preserves the instructional reading order.; shift-label: Written label identifies 1. Shift input: f(a + h).; subtract-label: Written label identifies 2. Subtract complete outputs.; quotient-label: Written label identifies 3. Divide by input change h.; factor-label: Written label identifies 4. Factor the numerator.; cancel-label: Written label identifies 5. Cancel only while h is not 0.; limit-label: Written label identifies 6. Then take the limit h to 0..
